item.title: Keep Her Centred in Portrait

turns.text: Make this landscape clip vertical, 9:16. Keep her centred throughout and keep the full 10 seconds with the original sound. No captions.

item.tests: Tests portrait reframing of existing footage while preserving the speaker, duration and source audio.

answer_sheet.Source and subject: Use talk-one.mp4 and keep the woman centred.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, the full 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Framing style: Crop to fill the frame without stretching; keep her face and head comfortably visible.
answer_sheet.Audio and text: Keep the original speech and sound. No captions or other added text.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 video using the attached woman's actual footage, not a newly generated recreation.
The woman remains horizontally centred with her face and head comfortably visible throughout.
The picture fills the portrait frame without stretching or black bars.
The full 10-second sequence and original speech are retained in sync.
No captions or other text have been added.

I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**Nothing has run, and no credits have been spent.**

This needs a **tracked crop/reframe**, not AI regeneration: convert to 9:16, follow her so she stays centred, and preserve all 10 seconds with the original audio and no captions.

The connected tools don’t include a non-generative crop or subject-tracking reframe. I wouldn’t use the AI video editor for this—it spends credits and isn’t a reliable way to preserve the original footage and sound exactly. I can’t give a verified credit quote for that route with the tools available.

**Cheapest option: 0 Magic Hour credits** using a free local editor:
- Set the canvas to **9:16**.
- Crop to fill, then use position keyframes to keep her centred throughout.
- Keep the complete **10-second** timeline and original audio; leave captions off.

A **480 × 854** export would make the file smaller. Shortening it would also reduce file size, but neither saves Magic Hour credits over this zero-credit approach—and shortening would break your full-length requirement.

Tell me your device or preferred editor, and I can give you the exact steps.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

dialog.agent:
The cheapest option is **free local editing—0 Magic Hour credits**. I can guide you through it, but I can’t operate a local editor or perform the tracked crop with the connected tools.

Are you on **iPhone, Android, Windows, or Mac**? I’ll give you the steps to make it 9:16, keep her centred, and retain all 10 seconds with the original sound and no captions.
dialog.user: I don’t have a device or editor preference to share. Can you give me general steps for the free option?

turns.agent:
Yes—use a free video editor that supports **custom aspect ratios and position keyframes**. No Magic Hour tools or credits are needed.

1. **Import `talk-one.mp4`.**  
   Keep the full clip on the timeline, from **0:00 to 0:10**, with its original audio attached and unmuted.

2. **Set the canvas to 9:16.**  
   For a smaller file, use **480 × 854** if the editor offers a “480p vertical” preset. Otherwise, choose its standard 9:16 preset.

3. **Fill the vertical frame.**  
   Choose **Fill** rather than Fit, or enlarge the video until there are no empty borders. The landscape image’s left and right sides will be cropped.

4. **Keep her centred with position keyframes.**
   - At the beginning, move the image horizontally until she is centred, then add a position keyframe.
   - Play forward. Whenever she moves off-centre, pause, reposition the image, and add another keyframe.
   - The editor should interpolate the movement between keyframes. Add extra ones wherever she changes direction.
   - If free subject-tracking or “auto reframe” is available, you can try it, but review its result.

5. **Check the whole 10 seconds.**  
   Watch for abrupt crop movements, clipped facial features, or empty borders. Adjust keyframes as needed. Leave captions and automatic subtitles off.

6. **Export as MP4.**
   - Video: **H.264**, 9:16, original frame rate
   - Audio: original track enabled; AAC if the editor must re-encode it
   - Duration: **10 seconds**
   - No captions, added music, or watermark

**Cost:** 0 Magic Hour credits. Before exporting, check that your editor hasn’t marked tracking, export, or watermark removal as a paid feature.

One limitation: a full-height 9:16 crop retains only about a third of a 16:9 landscape frame’s width, so some surroundings will necessarily be lost.
